title: Does remote work empty the city centre?

turns.speaker: Hal
turns.text: Office occupancy midweek is around seventy per cent of what it was. Mondays and Fridays are nearer thirty.

turns.speaker: Jin
turns.text: And the sandwich shops built a business on five days that now has three.

turns.speaker: Vera
turns.text: Which is real, but it's a transfer rather than a loss. That lunch is being bought somewhere, just nearer where people live.

turns.speaker: Hal
turns.text: Except the somewhere is a suburb with a supermarket, not a small independent place.

turns.speaker: Vera
turns.text: Sometimes. The data on suburban high streets is actually quite positive, though. Smaller towns near big cities have done well out of this.

turns.speaker: Jin
turns.text: So the money didn't vanish, it moved outward.

turns.speaker: Vera
turns.text: Mostly, yes. Which is arguably what everyone wanted for thirty years of regional policy.

turns.speaker: Hal
turns.text: That's a fair point and an uncomfortable one for anyone who spent that career arguing for it.

turns.speaker: Jin
turns.text: The office buildings themselves are the harder question. You can't easily convert a deep-plan tower into flats.

turns.speaker: Vera
turns.text: Because the middle has no windows and the plumbing was never designed for it.

turns.speaker: Hal
turns.text: The conversions that do work tend to be older, narrower buildings, which is a nice irony.

turns.speaker: Jin
turns.text: And the public transport is priced on five-day commuting that no longer exists.

turns.speaker: Vera
turns.text: Which is fixable with fares, and is being fixed extremely slowly.

points: Midweek office occupancy is around seventy per cent of pre-existing levels, with Mondays and Fridays near thirty.
City centre businesses built around five-day attendance have suffered.
Vera argues this is a transfer rather than a loss, with spending moving closer to where people live.
Data on suburban and small-town high streets has been positive, which arguably fulfils decades of regional policy aims.
Converting deep-plan office towers to housing is difficult because of windowless interiors and unsuitable plumbing, while older narrower buildings convert well.
Public transport pricing still assumes five-day commuting and is adapting slowly.
